personas.name: Sage
personas.description: Calm, unhurried, philosophical. Speaks in short sentences and lets silence do the work. Never panics, never flatters.
voice_rules: Short declarative sentences.
Asks one question at a time.
References long-term identity, not short-term feeling.
Never uses exclamation marks.
Paraphrases Stoic ideas (Marcus Aurelius, Epictetus, Seneca) without direct quotation.

personas.name: Coach
personas.tagline: Urge isn't an instruction. Give it ten minutes.
personas.description: Blunt but on your side. Talks like a good strength coach: clear instructions, zero drama, celebrates effort not talk.
voice_rules: Imperatives. 'Stand up.' 'Ten minutes.' 'Go.'
Never shames. Corrects the action, respects the person.
Uses training metaphors sparingly.
Occasional dry humor.
Ends with a next action.

personas.name: Grace
personas.tagline: Come back to God for a minute.
personas.description: Warm and steady. Speaks from faith without preaching. Points the user toward prayer, Scripture, gratitude and rest.
voice_rules: Gentle, never condemning. Grace is in the name.
Scripture references only from public-domain translations (KJV / WEB), always with book chapter:verse in source.
Invites rather than commands: 'Would you pray with me for a moment?'
Never claims God's punishment or guarantees outcomes.
Allowed to be quietly funny.

personas.name: Sunny
personas.description: Bright, silly, kind. Interrupts heavy days with small joys. Still holds you to your word, but with a grin.
voice_rules: Light and fast. Jokes land in one line.
Notices small good things: weather, water, a stretch.
Accountability delivered as a wink, not a lecture.
Never sarcastic at the user's expense.
Uses at most one emoji per Moment, often none.

personas.name: Brother
personas.tagline: I've got you. Now get up.
personas.description: The friend who tells you the truth and then buys you lunch. Casual, loyal, slightly teasing, always there.
voice_rules: Casual speech. 'Bro', 'man', 'look' are fine, no slurs, no crude sexual talk.
Teases gently, then backs you.
Talks about real life: work, money, family, the gym, sleep.
Admits his own struggles occasionally ('I've been there').
Ends with 'I'm here' energy, not pressure.

personas.name: Future Me
personas.description: Your own voice from years ahead. Only speaks from your recorded Future Self messages and long-horizon perspective.
voice_rules: First person, past tense about today's choices.
Never invents specifics about the user's future.
Primarily delivers user-recorded messages.

claims.claim: Sperm production is a continuous process. A full cycle of spermatogenesis takes roughly two to two-and-a-half months, so sperm are not simply stored up indefinitely from the moment ejaculation stops.
claims.review_note: Title to be confirmed by the medical reviewer against the PubMed record.

claims.claim: Longer ejaculatory abstinence tends to increase semen volume and the total number of sperm available in an ejaculate.
claims.source_title: Revisiting the relationship between the ejaculatory abstinence period and semen characteristics (Int J Fertil Steril, 2018)

claims.claim: Longer abstinence does not mean every measure of sperm quality keeps improving. Longer intervals have been associated with lower progressive motility and higher sperm DNA fragmentation, while shorter intervals can be preferable for those measures.
claims.source_title: PubMed 38828413 - ejaculatory abstinence, motility and sperm DNA fragmentation (2024)
claims.review_note: Supported also by PubMed 41809803 (2026) and 29143943 (2018). Titles to be confirmed by the medical reviewer.

claims.claim: The WHO laboratory manual asks for 2 to 7 days of ejaculatory abstinence before a semen sample. That is a laboratory standardisation window so results can be compared, not a recommendation that anyone should retain semen for health.
claims.source_title: WHO laboratory manual for the examination and processing of human semen, 6th edition (2021)

claims.claim: An individual's sperm concentration, count, motility and morphology can only be measured by a laboratory semen analysis. No app timer can estimate them.
claims.source_title: WHO laboratory manual for the examination and processing of human semen, 6th edition (2021)

claims.claim: Male ageing is associated with declines in semen volume, motility, progressive motility, normal morphology and DNA integrity. A large meta-analysis did not find a consistent decline in sperm concentration with age, so there is no universal fixed percentage decline per year.
claims.source_title: Consistent age-dependent declines in human semen quality: a systematic review and meta-analysis (Ageing Research Reviews, 2015)

claims.claim: Individual studies have estimated different age effects on semen quality, including some that reported declines in concentration. Results differ enough that a single regression formula should not be applied to every man.
claims.source_title: PubMed 16225533 - age and semen parameters, single-population study
claims.review_note: Title and year to be confirmed by the medical reviewer.

claims.claim: There is no strong evidence that abstaining from ejaculation raises testosterone in a lasting way. One small study reported a short-term fluctuation around day seven of abstinence that then returned toward baseline; it has not been replicated at scale.
claims.source_title: A research on the relationship between ejaculation and serum testosterone level in men (J Zhejiang Univ Sci, 2003)
claims.review_note: n=28. Frequently over-cited online; present only as limited evidence.

claims.claim: Claims that semen retention produces supernatural energy, magnetism or special powers come from tradition and personal testimony, not from controlled scientific evidence.
claims.review_note: Displayed with the white 'tradition' label only.

claims.claim: Urges rise, peak and pass on their own within minutes. Practising 'urge surfing', noticing the urge without acting, has been shown to reduce acting on cravings.
claims.source_title: Surfing the urge: brief mindfulness-based intervention for college student smokers (Psychology of Addictive Behaviors, 2009)
claims.review_note: Studied in smoking; generalisation to sexual urges is reasonable but indirect.

claims.claim: Poor or short sleep is associated with weaker self-control and more impulsive decisions the following day.
claims.source_title: Interactions between sleep habits and self-control (Frontiers in Human Neuroscience, 2015)

claims.claim: Regular physical exercise is associated with better mood and gains in self-regulation that carry over into other areas of life.
claims.source_title: Longitudinal gains in self-regulation from regular physical exercise (British Journal of Health Psychology, 2006)

claims.claim: Even mild dehydration can worsen mood, concentration and the feeling of effort in healthy adults.
claims.source_title: Mild dehydration impairs cognitive performance and mood of men (British Journal of Nutrition, 2011)

claims.claim: New habits take weeks to months to become automatic, and the time varies widely between people. Missing a single day does not undo the habit.
claims.source_title: How are habits formed: modelling habit formation in the real world (European Journal of Social Psychology, 2010)
claims.review_note: Median 66 days; range 18 to 254 days. Never show the number as a promise.

claims.claim: Deciding in advance exactly what you will do when a trigger appears ('If it is 11 PM and I am scrolling, then I put the phone in the kitchen') reliably improves follow-through on goals.
claims.source_title: Implementation intentions and goal achievement: a meta-analysis of effects and processes (Advances in Experimental Social Psychology, 2006)

claims.claim: Sperm DNA fragmentation tends to increase with age. This is one of the reproductive parameters most consistently linked to ageing.
claims.source_title: Consistent age-dependent declines in human semen quality: a systematic review and meta-analysis (Ageing Research Reviews, 2015)

claims.claim: In some fertility-treatment settings, shorter abstinence intervals have been associated with better outcomes for motility and DNA integrity. Anyone planning a pregnancy should follow their clinician's advice rather than an app.
claims.source_title: PubMed 41809803 - abstinence interval and fertility outcomes (2026)
claims.review_note: Title to be confirmed by the medical reviewer.

lessons.title: What actually happens to sperm when you don't ejaculate?

blocks.text: Sperm production never stops. Your testes run a continuous production line, and one full cycle from stem cell to mature sperm takes roughly two to two-and-a-half months.
When you don't ejaculate, sperm that are not released are reabsorbed by the body or passed during nocturnal emissions. Nothing accumulates forever, and nothing 'backs up'.
Longer abstinence does increase the volume of a later ejaculate and the number of sperm in it.
This app tracks your commitment precisely. It does not, and cannot, track what is happening inside your body.
This is the most repeated claim online, so it deserves a straight answer: the evidence is weak.
The study everyone quotes followed a small group of men for a short period. It observed a short-lived fluctuation, not a lasting rise, and it has not been replicated at scale.
Claims about energy, magnetism or special powers are tradition and testimony, not measurement.
If you practise retention, do it for your own reasons: discipline, faith, focus, relationships. You don't need a hormone myth to justify a personal commitment.

lessons.title: Why can urges suddenly become intense?

blocks.text: Urges are waves. They build, crest, and fall, usually within a few minutes, whether or not you act on them.
Three things make the wave feel bigger: tiredness, being alone with a screen late at night, and boredom. Two of those you can change tonight.
Deciding in advance what you'll do when the wave hits works better than deciding in the moment.
Urge Mode in this app is built around exactly this: don't decide anything yet, give it ten minutes, change what your body is doing.

lessons.title: How does male fertility change with age?

blocks.text: Men keep producing sperm throughout life, but several measures shift with age.
Semen volume, motility, morphology and DNA integrity tend to decline. Concentration, the number of sperm per millilitre, did not decline consistently across a very large body of studies.
Individual studies disagree about how much and how fast, which is why this app will never show you a 'percent decline per year'.
Your body changes with time. So should the way you look after it: sleep, movement, weight, alcohol and smoking all matter more than any timer.

lessons.title: What does a semen analysis actually measure?

blocks.text: A laboratory semen analysis measures volume, sperm concentration, total count, motility, morphology and sometimes DNA fragmentation.
Those numbers cannot be estimated from your age or from how many days you've abstained. Any app that shows you a live sperm count is making it up.
If you want a real picture of your reproductive health, ask a clinician for a semen analysis. That is the appropriate measurement.

lessons.title: What does the WHO 2 to 7 day interval mean?

blocks.text: You may have read that the WHO 'recommends' 2 to 7 days of abstinence. It does, but only before a laboratory sample.
The window exists so that results from different men and different labs can be compared fairly. It is not health advice about how often anyone should ejaculate.
Your commitment length is a personal choice, not a medical prescription.
Not for every measure. Longer abstinence tends to raise volume and count, but research has linked longer intervals with lower progressive motility and more DNA fragmentation.
In some fertility clinics, shorter intervals are actually preferred for that reason.
So the biology is a trade-off, not a ladder. That is why Alter Ego frames retention as a commitment you choose, not a health score you climb.
The version of you at 1 AM after five hours of sleep makes different decisions from the version at 9 AM after eight.
If most of your resets happen late at night, the most effective intervention might not be willpower. It might be an earlier bedtime and a phone that sleeps in another room.
Journey will show you the time of day your chapters tend to end. Use it.
Habits form over weeks and months, and the timeline varies enormously between people.
In the research on habit formation, missing a single day made no measurable difference to the long-term outcome. What mattered was returning.
Movement helps too: regular exercise has been linked to gains in self-regulation that spill over into unrelated areas.
That is why Alter Ego counts chapters, not streaks, and shows committed days out of total days rather than resetting you to zero.

lessons.title: Another year: what changes with male reproductive ageing?

blocks.text: Every birthday, Alter Ego will nudge you to read this rather than show you a made-up decline number.
The measures most consistently affected by age are motility, morphology and DNA integrity. The strongest levers you control are sleep, body weight, exercise, alcohol and smoking.
If you are planning children and are over 35, a conversation with a clinician is worth more than any timer.

timeline.disclaimer: This timeline describes what research says about ejaculatory abstinence in general. It cannot measure your body. Individual semen quality can only be measured by a laboratory semen analysis.

phases.title: Reset & Recovery
phases.summary: Your reproductive system continues producing sperm continuously. Nothing has been 'lost' and nothing needs to be 'rebuilt'.

phases.title: Short Abstinence
phases.summary: Semen volume and the number of sperm available at ejaculation may begin increasing.

phases.title: Continued Abstinence
phases.summary: Longer abstinence is generally associated with greater semen volume and count. Other parameters do not necessarily improve. This is also the window laboratories use to standardise samples.

phases.title: Longer Abstinence
phases.summary: More abstinence does not automatically mean 'better sperm'. Research has associated longer intervals with trade-offs, including lower progressive motility and higher DNA fragmentation. Your commitment is your own; the biology is not a scoreboard.
